about: Civ4's screens, from the main menu to the screens and popups of a game, how to reach each one and where its controls are, explored on 2026-11-11 at 1920x1080 windowed (a 1926x1120 window). Each control has its window-relative xy, the screen it leads to (to) when clicked, and a short note; a screen's tests list keys or clicks tried and what they did, while the story behind them, quirks and failed tries are in README_Game_Runs.md; controls marked 'not clicked' have real effects, such as starting a game, switching mod, going online or closing Civ4, and were left alone. desktop_windows.py click --point SCREEN.CONTROL clicks one, such as single_player.load_game. Menu items sit at x 965 from y 575, 45 px apart. Each control sits on one line so the screens read like tables. These positions change with the resolution or the mod's UI code; re-check them with check_points.py after such a change.
shortcuts_about: Every key from the Sevopedia's Shortcuts pages, read from Assets/XML/Text/AdvCiv-SAS_Sevopedia_Lengthy.xml when this file is generated; "chipotle" entries need CheatCode = chipotle in CivilizationIV.ini, which the user's has. Keys reach Civ4 through desktop_windows.py key and type, whose events carry scan codes.

tests: ctrl+left, ctrl+right
rotate the camera 45 degrees and back
f10, then enter
open the capital's city screen, then leave it
alt+i
hides the whole interface; a second alt+i restores it
pgup, pgdn
no zoom change, with or without the extended-key flag
mouse wheel over the map
zooms, only with Civ4 in front; from the farthest view +4 clicks show cities and borders, +6 to +8 a medium zoom with units readable, +10 close
c, num6 with no unit selected
nothing; after the city screen or advisors no unit is selected, so click one first
num6 with a Worker selected
did not move it
g, then a click on a tile
moves the selected unit there: a Worker centred by c at (960, 520) moved one tile east with a click at (1060, 520)
period, comma
select the next or previous unit in unit_bar, on the same tile
w
selected a group of about 8 units
click a unit in unit_bar
selected about 8 units at once, most likely the group it already belonged to
ctrl+click a unit in unit_bar
selected every unit of that type on the tile (11 of 11)
shift+click a second unit after a click
added it, and several more units, to the selection
alt+click a unit in unit_bar
selected nearly every unit on the tile; those left out had a grey dot rather than green, likely no moves left
backslash, as the US key code
moved one unit right in unit_bar, not back
ctrl+shift+x
opens autoplay_prompt; during a run it stops autoplay after 1 to 2 turns, then the held-back popups follow
ctrl+l
opens game_load_file
end_turn click
ended the turn (200 to 201); then popup_choose_research and popup_choose_production came
city_previous, then esc
a city selected on the main screen; esc returns to the unit
scoreboard scroll buttons (SAS48, Debug Mode)
down moves 1 row, down fast about 5; the list opens centred on the active player, so the top scorers (Justinian 248, Frederick 227) were hidden above until scrolled up
click the minimap
centres the view there; its lower right was open ocean on SAS48 Pangaea
click a foreign city's banner in Debug Mode
selects it on the main screen with its production choices, as city_previous does
click --double a foreign city's banner in Debug Mode
opens its city screen; the top bar then shows that player's research and gold
alt+click a leader on the scoreboard
opens popup_declare_war
g, then hover a far tile
draws the path with a numbered marker for each turn; a click gives the order and the selection moves to the next unit
click a plot with units
selects a unit there and can recentre the view, so re-read positions after each step
esc with no screen open
opens ingame_menu, even with a unit selected; with a popup open, the first esc closed that instead
b with a Settler selected
founds the city, then popup_city_name, popup_choose_research and popup_choose_production in turn
enter
ends the turn only when the end_turn circle is red, that is when no unit waits for orders; f (fortify) on the last idle unit made it red
hover or ctrl+z with a popup open
no help text, and Debug Mode did not toggle: popups take the input until answered
click a city banner (own)
selects the city with its production queue; a click on the city's buildings just above selected its units instead
hover an enemy city in Debug Mode
shows its food, production, build, gold and maintenance, not its units; --double opens its city screen with its buildings, such as Walls
mouse wheel while another window is in front
no zoom; bring Civ4 forward first (desktop_windows key pause does it harmlessly)
shift+enter
ends the turn, as the end_turn button does; a new tech then opened popup_tech_discovered
ctrl+z
Debug Mode on, revealing the whole map; again turns it off (needs CheatCode = chipotle)
in-game autoplay running: Civ4 in the background, then in front
it kept playing either way, about 20 turns per 15 s; focus does not pause it
f3 during autoplay
the Foreign Diplomacy Advisor opened on Relations and stayed open while turns kept passing; esc closed it, autoplay still running
ctrl+z on and off during autoplay
Debug Mode toggled without stopping autoplay
ctrl+shift+x during autoplay
stopped it; here an AI won a Domination victory the same turn, so popup_victory came next
click a city banner with a unit selected
nothing: the click did not reach the banner; city_previous and city_next selected the city instead
city selected on the main screen: click a production choice, then a queue row
the choice went to the queue's front and onto the city's banner (Stable (8)); clicking its queue row (y about 962, rows 30 px apart) removed it: production can be changed without entering the city
the next-unit button left of the city arrows, clicked repeatedly
selects the next unit still waiting for orders, centring the map on it each time, across ships and land units; 44 presses brought the first unit round again in this game
g with a Privateer selected, then a click on a fogged sea tile
drew the path into the fog with a turn marker and gave the order; the selection then moved to the next unit
click the Great Person bar (top middle)
opened the city screen of the city it names (Eridu)
click a city banner while one of our units is selected
nothing; esc then opened ingame_menu instead of deselecting; after cancelling it a click selected the city, and a double-click opened its city screen, a foreign city too in Debug Mode
zoom level for clicking banners
at the farthest zooms banners are tiny and each click recentred the map; 4 wheel clicks in from far made them easy targets and readable

tests: esc
closes the advisor
reopening an advisor
it opens on the tab last used: F3 on Espionage after Ctrl+E
f1, f3 in Debug Mode
each gains debug_player_dropdown
f2, Tribalism, REVOLUTION
"Autoplay adopts Tribalism! (Abolishes Slavery.)" on the main screen, at once
f5_map_show_units
turns into Hide individual units and lists each unit with strength, moves, XP and promotion icons
Map tab: click a unit row, then another leader, without and with Debug Mode

the row turns yellow; without Debug Mode another leader's list is empty; with it, that leader's units are listed, the world map is revealed, and the selected type's units show as yellow dots on the map
Map tab: click a unit type row, then ctrl+click and shift+click others
both modifiers add the type to the selection (rows turn yellow) and the map dots show all selected types; rows 32 px apart from y 218 at x 850 in this game
f1 or f2 in Debug Mode: choose another player
their cities and data show; double-clicking a foreign city's row in F1 does not open it
find another player's city with a corporation
F2 Corporations with that player chosen names the cities; minimap click toward their colour, zoom in, then click the banner

f1_domestic.note: Domestic Advisor: tabs Overview 1, Overview 2, Overview 3, Overview 4, Finance; a city table

f2_policy.note: Policy Advisor: tabs Civics, Religions, Corporations; civic columns Government, Legal, Labor, Economy, Religion

f3_diplomacy.note: Foreign Diplomacy Advisor: tabs Relations, Glance, Info, Espionage; a web of leader portraits

f4_trade.note: Foreign Trade Advisor: tabs Treaties, Bonuses, Techs, Cities; one row per civilization

f5_military.note: Military Advisor: tabs Summary, Map, Battles, Composition along y 1090 (Map at x 430, Battles at x 668)

f5_map_leaders.note: Map tab: leader portraits in rows of 10, about 68 px apart, the Barbarian skull last; a click lists that player's units on the right, grouped by combat type, with a Show individual units checkbox; the world map below

f5_battles_player.note: Battles tab, Debug Mode: a player dropdown; items 26 px apart from y 132 at x 100; the table lists that player's battles with turn, odds, units, XP and plot; LOG and Legend at the top right; clicking a row showed no change

f6_technology.note: Technology Advisor: the tech tree, no tabs

f7_world.note: World Advisor: tabs BFC 1, BFC 2, Territory, Environment, Changes

f8_info.note: Info Screen: tabs Graph, Score, Timeline, Demographics, Top 5 Cities/Wonders, Statistics

f9_victory.note: Victory Screen: tabs Victories, Settings, Resolutions, Members

ctrl_e_espionage.note: opens the Foreign Diplomacy Advisor on its Espionage tab

debug_player_dropdown.note: in Debug Mode only: a wide dropdown at the top left of F1 and F3, likely choosing whose data the advisor shows; its items were not read yet

f2_religions.note: Religions: one religion per column at the top with founded, holy city, leader and influence; a city table below

f2_corporations.note: Corporations tab: one column per corporation, 177 px apart from x 286 (built by, consumes, generates, founded, HQ); the player's cities below in two lists, those with a corporation marked by its icon and yield; in Debug Mode the player dropdown at (176, 96) switches whose cities show, items 23 px apart from y 134; clicking a city name does nothing

f2_civic_columns.note: Civics tab: Government, Legal, Labor, Economy and Religion columns 300 px apart from x 90 (names at x 90, 390, 690, 990, 1290), civics 30 px apart from y 196; an icon marks the ones available; a click previews it below and turns the bottom bar into CANCEL (x 752) and REVOLUTION (x 1398)

f2_revolution.note: after choosing civics: adopts them and closes the advisor; with 0 turns for revolution there was no anarchy

f1_table.note: Overview 1-4: one city per row from y 162, 24 px apart, headings at y 138; Overview 1 ends with Producing, Overview 4 with the city's X and Y

f1_legend.note: Legend at the top right, as on several advisors

f1_finance_rates.note: Finance: rate buttons beside Research, Culture, Espionage and Gold, at x 50 and 72, 30 px apart from y 740; the treasury line at y 420

f3_relations_legend.note: Relations: line colours for contact, war, defensive pact, open borders, team and vassal at the bottom left

f3_espionage_weights.note: Espionage: one leader per row about 56 px apart with + and - weight buttons; cities, passive effects and missions with costs to the right

f5_map_show_units.note: Map: the Show individual units checkbox above the unit list

f5_battles_table.note: Battles: headings at y 140, rows 24 px apart from y 164; Turn sorted ascending, then descending; LOG at (1394, 94)

f8_graph_dropdowns.note: Graph: two dropdowns at the top left, the measure (Score) and the time span (Entire timeline)

f8_timeline_log.note: Timeline: LOG at the top right; the event list scrolls

f8_score_table.note: Score: one leader per row; a heading click re-sorts

f9_space_view.note: Victories: the space race's View button

exit_tab.note: EXIT, the last tab of every advisor

tech_tree.reach: F6, or the Technology Advisor button at (1790, 79); EXIT at (1660, 1090)
tech_tree.shows: the tech tree: known techs green, available ones lavender, out of reach blue; the queue position and turns before a queued tech's name, such as 1 Professional Army (1); a bottom strip shows which techs each Great Person could discover
tests: click an available tech's title (Banking)
replaced the whole queue with the path to it: 1 Broader Education (4), 2 Banking (5); the current tech dropped out but kept its progress
click the dropped tech again, then shift+click Banking
1 Professional Army (1), 2 Broader Education (4), 3 Banking (5): Shift appends the path
click an unlock icon inside a tech box
nothing opened
click an already known tech (Fishing)
clears all research, as the user said; the top bar then shows one icon per available tech instead of the research bar
great_people_techs icons
the lightbulb shows techs Great People could discover; each group to its right shows one Great Person type's current discovery or preference order, so they differ

tree.note: the wheel scrolls it sideways: 10 clicks down went from the classical to the industrial techs; click a tech's title

great_people_techs.note: lightbulb: techs Great People could discover; icon groups to its right, about x 110, 204, 320, 410, 504, show each Great Person type's current discovery and preference order

popup_victory.shows: X has won a ... Victory, with OK

ok.note: then come the replay, the Info Screen's graph, Your Place in History and the Hall of Fame, each with EXIT, and then popup_end_of_history

replay_screen.reach: end of a game, or hall_of_fame's V button from the main menu
replay_screen.shows: the map growing turn by turn, a score graph below it, and the game's event log on the right, which lists major events such as wars and city captures

play.note: PLAY, which becomes STOP while playing; plays to the end, about 10 s for 369 turns at default speed

next.note: NEXT advanced one replay turn in the early-game check

speed.note: speed slider from about x 822 to 1020, default near the left; after a drag to the left end the replay took about 8 s and after one to the right about 10 s, too close to tell which way is faster; the user thinks the far right is the fastest; re-test with a longer game

autoplay_prompt.shows: Turn on AI Auto Play? How many turns would you like the AI to control?

turns.note: prefilled with 501: click it, backspace 4 times, then type the count

ok.note: starts autoplay; 2 turns ran in under 3 s

game_load_file.shows: Load File: folder tree on the left, opened on Saves/single; saves on the right, newest first, with size and date

file_list.note: the first save; rows 24 px apart; one wheel click scrolls 3 rows; a click fills the filename

ok.note: loads the save: under 5 s for a turn-200 Standard game

popup_deal_cancelled.reach: an AI cancels a deal; came first after an interrupted autoplay
popup_deal_cancelled.shows: the diplomacy screen with the leader, both sides' items and one answer

popup_choose_production.reach: a city finished or can no longer build its item; came after an interrupted autoplay
popup_choose_production.shows: a list on the right: Examine City, then recommended and other items

items.note: items 40 px apart from here; a click sets the city's production

popup_choose_research.shows: What would you like to research next? Let's see the Big Picture, then techs with turns and recommendations

techs.note: the first tech; rows 36 px apart; a click sets research

popup_declare_war.reach: game_main: alt+click a leader on the scoreboard
popup_declare_war.shows: Does this mean WAR?!? (vs. the leader), and which third parties will disapprove

yes.note: Yes, DECLARE WAR!: on 2026-11-11 also cancelled open borders, and the enemy's city banners turned red

ingame_menu.shows: Exit to Desktop, Exit to Main Menu, Retire, Load Game, Save Game, Options, BUG Menu, Enter WorldBuilder, Game Details, Your Details, Cancel

items.note: the first item, Exit to Desktop; items 31 px apart; at the start of a game Regenerate Map appears fourth and pushes the later items down a row; the exits, Retire and WorldBuilder have real effects

exit_to_main_menu.note: the second item in both layouts

popup_tech_discovered.reach: a tech is discovered at the start of a turn
popup_tech_discovered.shows: the tech's quote, special abilities, what it leads to and allows

exit_to_main_menu.note: leaves the game without asking to save; the main menu came back within 8 s

popup_city_name.shows: What would you like to name this settlement? with the suggested name

ok.note: keeps the name; the first city then asked for research, then production

popup_civic_available.reach: a new civic becomes available, such as Pacifism at a Renaissance start
popup_civic_available.shows: Would you like to start a revolution?

no.note: No, the old ways are best

popup_first_unit.reach: the first unit of a new kind is trained, such as the first Camel Knight
popup_first_unit.shows: Congratulations, you have trained your first ... unit, with what it does

popup_vote_result.reach: a vote in the Apostolic Palace or United Nations ends
popup_vote_result.shows: the resolution, the result and each civilization's vote
